title: Rework lazy shard merger and tokenizer synchronizer
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Rework the model asset activation path to replace the current eager shard merge step that causes peak memory spikes with a progressive shard merger and introduce a lightweight tokenizer synchronizer handshake to ensure consistent tokenizer mappings across model variants during hot-reloads. Goals: reduce peak host memory during multi-gpu shard activation by >=30%, eliminate race conditions between tokenizer init and KV cache activation, simplify compatibility hooks for legacy weight formats, and make the activation path observable and feature-flag controlled. Scope: runtime loader logic, shard-merging policy, mmap usage, tokenizer init handshake, unit and e2e tests, integration with Canary rollout and Dedicated nodes. Out of scope: model training exporters and offline conversion tooling.
comments: 2025-02-10 Priya Nair: Created ticket after memory regression seen in canary-ingest (regression started 2025-01-28). Attached heap snapshots and timeline where shard-merge peaks at 88GB for 2xA100 activation of the 30B endpoint.

2025-02-12 Alex Morgensen: Spike repro steps and local script added. Observed duplication of weight pages when merge() runs while tokenizer initializes. Hypothesis: current merge implementation copies pages then maps them; progressive activation can instead map readonly pages and apply atomic remap to reduce duplication.

2025-02-18 Daniel Cho (review): Reviewed mmap strategy. Agreed to upgrade 'mmap-utils' to 2.4.1 to get the MAP_SHARED_VALIDATE fallback; flagged a kernel compatibility note for on-prem customers. Added dependency to ENG-47109 (kernel compatibility matrix).

2025-02-20 Maria Lopez: Added functional tests outline and suggested to include a randomized race test that toggles tokenizer load order and simulates KV cache warmups. Also recommended adding telemetry for 'activation_duration_ms' and 'activation_peak_rss_mb'.

2025-02-24 Alex Morgensen: Prototype branch pushed: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872. Prototype shows 34% reduction in peak RSS for the 30B model in our benchmark harness. Still failing two unit tests related to legacy checkpoint manifest edge-cases.

2025-02-26 Elena Fischer: Performance digest attached: run-2025-02-25. Verified progressive merger reduces page fault churn; latency p50 unchanged, p99 improved by ~5% under concurrent warmup load. Noted increase in small syscalls due to on-demand mapping; suggest micro-optimizations after landing correctness.

2025-03-01 Samir Patel: Security review note: tokenizer synchronizer handshake does not introduce new network I/O; all exchanges are intra-process or via control-plane RPCs already allowed. No secrets in the handshake. Approve unless we expose stable tokenizer fingerprints to telemetry (opt-out).

2025-03-02 Priya Nair: Merged a fix for legacy manifest case. Preparing canary rollout in 'canary-0' cluster tomorrow. Plan: feature-flag enabled, 5% traffic to canary for 48h, monitor activation_peak_rss_mb, activation_duration_ms, and tokenization_error_rate.

Follow-ups: add migration note for customers on old checkpoint formats, add documentation in Console about new telemetry metrics, schedule a runtime-1.21 postmortem to record lessons and potential next optimizations.
